subject: Prod embeddings: p95/p99 latency spike after catalog rollout
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-team@nimbusanalytics.com
Date: 2027-08-10T09:12:00Z
Subject: Production embeddings latency problem — seeing p95/p99 regressions after your catalog rollout

Hi Stephanie,

We started seeing a sustained increase in embeddings latency around 07:15 UTC after your model catalog update this morning. Our ingestion pipeline (batching at 256) is seeing p95 jump from ~120ms to ~760ms and p99s up over 2s — causing backpressure and message queue growth. This is affecting search freshness for a subset of queries and triggering alerts.

Quick details:
- Region: us-west-2
- Endpoint: hosted.embeds/v1 (customer token)
- First spike observed: 2027-08-10T07:17:00Z

Can your team confirm if anything changed in the catalog or routing at ~07:00 UTC? We need an ETA on mitigation — rolling back to the previous model variant would be ideal if available.

Attaching screenshot of our Grafana panel and a short packet capture.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Search, Nimbus Analytics

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:25:00Z
Subject: Re: Production embeddings latency problem — seeing p95/p99 regressions after your catalog rollout

Hi Sarah — thanks for the heads up and the Grafana screenshot. Sorry you hit this. We're investigating immediately.

Immediate actions we can take right now:
- Route your traffic to the previous model variant (if you opt-in) — this is low-risk and can be done in ~10–15 minutes.
- Throttle large batch sizes server-side for your token quota to limit backpressure while we debug.

Neha (tech lead) and Marcus (AM) are looped in. Neha — can you pull the host traces for the timeframe Sarah mentioned and check for any catalog-related kernel dispatch or quantization changes?

I'll keep Sarah posted every 30 minutes until we have a mitigation.

— Stephanie
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T09:41:00Z
Subject: Re: Production embeddings latency problem — seeing p95/p99 regressions after your catalog rollout

Quick update from the infra side: I pulled traces and traces.zip (attached). Preliminary observations:
- Catalog switchover window ~2027-08-10T07:00:00Z.
- A new variant (v2-quant-opt) was promoted in the hosted catalog; traffic started shifting at ~07:03 UTC.
- The v2-quant-opt variant shows a subset of pods experiencing a CPU kernel fallback path that increases per-token latency for longer sequences; KV cache eviction events spike at the same time.

Hypothesis: mis-tagged quantized variant ended up using a slower fallback execution path on some hosts (driver/kernel mismatch). That would explain long-tailed p99s but not uniform p95 shifts. I'm starting a sweep to identify affected AZs and node images.

Attaching: trace_v2_20270810.zip (host traces), grafana_p95_p99_spike.png (panel).

Recommendation: Two options for immediate mitigation:
1) Temporary traffic split -> 100% to previous stable variant (rollback route). Low-risk, fast.
2) If rollback unacceptable, route 75% stable / 25% new to reduce p99 impact while we narrow hosts (slower).

I'll post a carrier update in 15m with which AZs are showing kernel fallbacks.

— Neha
Tech Lead, Inference Runtime

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Production embeddings latency problem — seeing p95/p99 regressions after your catalog rollout

Team — escalating to Eng: Monica, can you confirm whether an automated promotion pushed v2-quant-opt without the fallback flag in builds? Customer impact is visible and Nimbus is asking for rollback. Also flag for potential SLA credit discussion if we cannot meet the SLOs.

From a customer coordination perspective:
- If rollback is doable in the next 30–45 minutes, propose we take that path and notify Nimbus.
- If rollback requires more time, prepare a clear timeline and a compensating credit offer.

I'll stand by for the rollback plan and will coordinate comms with Sarah.

— Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Date: 2027-08-10T11:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Production embeddings latency problem — seeing p95/p99 regressions after your catalog rollout

Root cause and remediation summary:
- Root cause: During this morning's catalog rollout an internal tag mismatch caused the v2 quantized build to be marked as "quant-opt" while one of the host kernel images lacked the optimized quantized kernel. A subset of pods hit a slow fallback kernel path and experienced heavy KV-cache churn leading to long-tail latencies.
- Affected hosts: us-west-2a (primary), us-west-2c (partial).

Mitigation performed at 2027-08-10T11:05:00Z:
- We routed Nimbus traffic back to v1-stable variant (100% traffic).
- Killed affected pods and redeployed with corrected kernel compatibility checks.

Results: p95 returned to ~130ms and p99s dropped below 620ms within 8 minutes post-rollback (Grafana link below). We'll keep canary validation for 24 hours before re-promoting v2-quant-opt.

Next steps:
1) Post-mortem to be published within 72 hours.
2) Add an automated host-image compatibility gate to prevent mis-tagged promotions.
3) Offer customer 2 weeks of usage credits for downtime impact (Ops + AM to confirm).

Attachments: rollback_instructions.md (internal runbook snippet).

— Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-13T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Production embeddings latency problem — seeing p95/p99 regressions after your catalog rollout

Hi Sarah — following up with the final update. Monica's rollback completed successfully on Aug 10 and the service stabilized shortly after. Summary of actions and what we will deliver:

What we did:
- Rolled your traffic back to v1-stable (complete) and removed affected hosts.
- Deployed a compatibility gate and additional canary checks on catalog promotions.
- Performed a targeted re-run of your most common query shapes to validate p99 improvement.

What you can expect from us:
- Post-mortem document in 72 hours (will include timeline and mitigations).
- 2 weeks of usage credits applied to your account as a gesture for the regression.
- A follow-up call early next week to walk the PM and infra teams through the change and our canary plan.

Links: Grafana panel: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/embeds/prod?from=1691640000000&to=1691726400000
HubSpot ticket: HS-239482

If you'd like us to proactively pin your account to v1-stable for the next 48 hours, we can do that. Appreciate your patience and the quick signals from the Nimbus ops team.

Best,
— Stephanie
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
